verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at any level. The patch changes documentation wording only, mostly in text new in v19, and adds no syntax, GUC, catalog or behaviour change. Peter Smith and Matemática A3K approved v2 in the thread. One accuracy check remains for the committer: the reworded retention-limit note for retain_dead_tuples.

brief.title: Wording fixes for the create subscription reference page
brief.problem: Thom Brown found grammar and wording errors in the create subscription reference page, mostly in text for options new in v19. The target readers are users of logical replication who read that page.
brief.proposed_design: The patch changes wording only, in create_subscription.sgml. It edits text for the connect option, slot_name, binary, retain_dead_tuples and its retention limit, and two notes. The v2 patch from Laurenz Albe also drops "the" before "conflict detection" in the pg_conflict_detection notes of func-admin.sgml and protocol.sgml.
author_claims: The page has grammar errors, for example "if it does index scan" in the read-only subscribers scenario.
Masahiko Sawada says the fixes can be backpatched to v19, where most of the touched text was added.
brief.thread_state: Laurenz Albe posted a v2 patch with the agreed wording; Peter Smith and Matemática A3K approved it. Open questions are whether it goes into v19 before release and who commits it.
unclear: The material shows no v2 hunks, so the final wording of each change cannot be checked here.
The thread does not discuss the reworded retention-limit note for retain_dead_tuples, which changes meaning more than the other edits.
The thread does not say whether protocol.sgml was changed in v2; message #7 mentions only the function documentation.

Does v2 change protocol.sgml as well as func-admin.sgml, given that message #7 mentions only the function documentation?
Which v2 hunks apply to v19 and which only to master, if any touched text does not exist in v19?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the logical replication documentation, in particular the retain_dead_tuples text; the visible thread shows no committer taking the patch.
committability.liability: Small: wording in three documentation files. The one item to sign for is that the reworded retention-limit note still describes server behaviour.
committability.author_follow_up: Thom Brown answered the review the same day in message #3 and accepted most of the suggested changes.

priority.reason: The patch is about 5 KiB of wording fixes in documentation read by users of logical replication, and reviewers approved v2. It needs a committer to pick it up for v19.

precedents_retrieved.title: add subscription TAP test option "vcregress subscriptioncheck" for MSVC builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a "subscriptioncheck" option to vcregress.pl so that MSVC builds can run the subscription TAP tests with one command, like "recoverycheck". Later the thread moved to a documentation patch that describes "vcregress taptest" for Windows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan objected to adding more special targets to vcregress.pl, because the generic taptest option already runs any TAP test set with "vcregress taptest src/test/subscription". The author agreed and switched to a documentation patch. Juan José Santamaría Flecha reviewed that patch and asked for a typo fix and new wording, and the visible messages show no revised version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:

vcregress.pl rather than add more.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab-completion refactoring and word-removal feature (was IF-NOT_EXISTS for tab-completion)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set refactors psql_completion by moving the macros to a new header and turning the long else-if chain into standalone ifs in a separate function. On top of that it adds word-shift and word-removal macros, keyword case that follows input, and suggestions for IF (NOT) EXISTS, OR REPLACE and other syntax.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers judged the refactoring too large and not worth the trouble so soon after the 9.6 rewrite of tab completion; Tom Lane's objection about back-patching appears only in quoted lines. Michael Paquier proposed a localized way to add IF (NOT) EXISTS through words_after_create. The author said removing the else chain is the core of the patch, so a localized patch means abandoning it, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The general consensus seems to be that this feature is too large
a rewrite of tab completion considering a major rewrite was done for 9.6.

precedents_retrieved.title: Detection and resolution of logical replication conflict
precedents_retrieved.authors: Zhijie Hou (houzj), shveta malik (shvetam), Nisha Moond (nishamoond)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal adds conflict detection and resolution to the logical replication apply worker, with conflict types such as insert_exists, update_origin_differs, update_missing and delete_missing. Users pick a built-in resolver (for example apply_remote, keep_local, skip, error or last_update_wins) per conflict type, first as a global setting and later as a CONFLICT RESOLVER clause on CREATE SUBSCRIPTION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The patch set was still under review at v17 in October 2024, and the last message shown, from 2024-10-28, has no reply. Two items were still open at that point: clock-skew handling, and a race in which DirtySnapshot index scans miss rows and report update_missing or delete_missing instead of the origin_differs conflicts.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reworks the SELECT reference page so that join syntax is more prominent, adding a separate recursive join_expression element to the FROM clause synopsis. It also moves the LATERAL description above the join parameters.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix documentation and logging for START_REPLICATION
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds logical decoding on physical standbys. It includes timeline following for logical slots, separate catalog_xmin in hot standby feedback, no snapshot export on standby, a hot_standby_feedback requirement, and slot cleanup on database drop. (The thread title differs from the entry title.)
precedents_retrieved.objection: In April 2017 Robert Haas moved the entry to the next commitfest after an exchange with Andres Freund, and Craig Ringer agreed; that exchange is not shown. Known gaps stayed open, including detecting when the upstream has removed catalog tuples the standby needs. In December 2017 the author put the work aside for other work, and the visible messages show no later revision before the withdrawal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I've had to backburner this due to other work.

precedents_retrieved.title: DOCS - Generated Column Logical Replication Examples
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an "Examples" subsection to the new "Generated Column Replication" documentation section. The examples are self-contained publication, subscription and table setups that show subtle rules, such as publication column lists overriding publish_generated_columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the opening message is shown, and the entry was later withdrawn without any visible reply or objection.

precedents_retrieved.title: Build the docs if there are changes in docs and don't run other tasks if the changes are only in docs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the docs build out of the CompilerWarnings CI task into its own Cirrus task, which runs only when files under doc/, files that feed the docs, or the CI files change. Later versions skip all CI tasks when a change touches only README files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued the change would rarely apply: few README-only patches reach a commit fest, manual pushes to a personal CI should not be second-guessed, and buildfarm runs batch several commits. He also noted reverse dependencies, such as psql help built from DocBook sources, that make docs-only detection hard. The author agreed and withdrew; the README exclusion went into the buildfarm sample config instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think unless some concrete reason for this change can be shown, we
should drop it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
Reverted commit(s): Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add GROUP BY ALL".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add GROUP BY ALL".
Reverted commit(s): Add GROUP BY ALL.; Update GROUP BY ALL comments about window functions
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit ef38a4d9756db9ae1d20f40aa39f3cf76059b81a which
implemented the GROUP BY ALL syntax, as well as 2ce745836 which
made some comment improvements therein.

A postcommit review discovered that GROUP BY ALL missed our special
handling of entries that also appear in an ORDER BY in the query.
This caused the query to return wrong results when ORDER BY
specifies non-default equality semantics.  While this should be
fixable with some refactoring, doing it cleanly seems like too
much code churn for late beta.  We'll revert and try again in v20.

The reverted commit also included some additional comment wordsmithing
and docs cleanup, which are retained as they weren't connected to the
reverted feature.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found, and the thread points to no earlier discussion of these edits. The patch is a docs-only wording fix for text new in v19, and three reviewers approved v2, so no earlier rejection reason applies.

The patch changes documentation wording only. It adds no syntax, keyword, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour or dump content, so no existing query, script, dump or client behaves differently after upgrade. The reworded retention-limit note for retain_dead_tuples should be checked against server behaviour, but that is a documentation accuracy question outside this angle.

The patch changes documentation wording only, so it touches no on-disk format, WAL, replication protocol, catalog, wire protocol or extension ABI. The retention-limit note for retain_dead_tuples describes replication behaviour, but whether the new wording is accurate is a docs question for another angle.

The patch changes wording only in documentation for create subscription, func-admin and protocol pages. It adds no privilege, default, exposure path or denial-of-service surface, and the one wording change about access control between subscriber and publisher was reverted to the original in message #7.

The patch changes documentation wording only. It adds no hot-path cost, no API, no catalog entry and no external dependency, and it leaves no new place that later features must update. From the maintenance angle there is nothing to object to. One check remains open for whoever commits it: the reworded retention-limit note for retain_dead_tuples should still match server behaviour.
The patch fixes grammar and wording in existing reference pages. No existing feature, extension or external tool can fix wording in the core documentation, so nothing from this angle applies.

The patch fixes grammar and wording in user-facing reference docs, mostly in text new in v19. Every reader of the create subscription page gains, and it adds no maintenance cost, GUC, catalog change or user interface, so the demand question does not apply. Four people reviewed or approved it in the thread.
